title: Statuspage update: compact reassurance and operator checks
abstract: Compact customer-facing status update with a short timeline, immediate mitigation steps customers can take, a lightweight verification checklist for tenant operators, and FAQs. Designed for a short statuspage entry plus follow-up postmortem addendum.
body:
Executive summary:

On 2026-05-14 starting at ~09:23 UTC we observed a regionally scoped latency surface affecting a subset of tenant inference requests in the us-west cluster. The platform continued to serve most traffic, but a small percentage (~2–5%) of requests experienced increased tail latency and occasional stalled streaming responses. No data loss or model corruption was detected. Root cause analysis is ongoing; timeline and mitigations below.

Impact (short):
- Affected tenants: small fraction of production tenants primarily in us-west (tenants with long-context chat workloads and streaming enabled).
- Symptom: elevated p95/p99 latency and sporadic streaming stalls (clients saw longer-than-usual response times or streaming freeze for 3–15s).
- Duration: intermittent between 09:23–12:10 UTC with an initial mitigation at 10:05 UTC and a stopgap routing change at 11:40 UTC. We consider the incident resolved for most tenants as of 12:10 UTC.

What we did (customer-facing chronology):
- 09:23 UTC: automated latency alert triggered; ops paged.
- 09:30–10:00 UTC: first investigations pointed to a change in KV-cache eviction patterns on a specific GPU pool combined with an unbalanced request mix; replication and cache warm paths were slower.
- 10:05 UTC: we pushed a throttled cache warming and KV prefetch patch to the affected pool (rollback-safe). Immediate improvement for many workloads, p95 reduced by ~40% for short sequences.
- 11:40 UTC: as a precaution we enabled temporary cross-pool routing for streaming sessions that satisfied latency constraints, diverting new sessions away from the impacted pool. This stopped most stalls for new requests.
- 12:10 UTC: monitoring returned to baseline for the overwhelming majority of tenants. We maintained extra routing and cache warmers for 8 hours afterward.

Customer actions you can take (self-serve checklist):
- If you saw stalled streaming responses, try resuming the session with a fresh connection (open a new streaming session). This avoids the degraded session KV-state.
- If you rely on long-context sessions, set a short reconnect policy client-side (3–5s) and use idempotent client tokens so retries do not duplicate intent.
- For tenants that saw any truncated structured output: request a replay with the same input + model/version via our replay endpoint (see linked artifact CONFLUENCE-Page-ID-12345 for replay instructions).
- If you want us to proactively verify your tenant’s recent traces, open a support ticket with the subject: "Verify traces from 2026-05-14 us-west latency surface" and include tenant id.

Operator verification checklist (for tenant SRE/devs):
- Verify streaming reconnect behavior: open two short streams in succession, confirm streaming handshake latency <200ms from us-west.
- Check last successful response timestamp vs recent requests; if gaps >30s, escalate.
- Confirm replay of 3 representative requests succeeds with identical outputs (if deterministic for your workflow).
- Run a small burst test (50 requests at production concurrency) during off-peak window to confirm p95 < your SLAs.

Current status and next steps: 
- Status: resolved for most tenants; monitoring on watch for 48 hours.
- Next steps we are executing: continuing root cause analysis (we are collecting KV-cache eviction traces and runtime scheduling logs), comprehensive post-incident RCA to be published within 5 business days, and a technical addendum for tenants with long-context streaming usage explaining permanent mitigations and recommended client patterns.

Root cause hypothesis (working):
- We saw an interaction between (a) aggressive KV-cache eviction on an older kernel on a portion of the us-west GPU pool, (b) a spike of long-context streaming sessions that caused disproportionate context loading, and (c) our continuous-batching scheduler briefly favoring throughput for short sequences which amplified eviction churn. The combination increased cache miss amplification and introduced stall windows for some streaming sessions.

Temporary mitigation already applied:
- KV prefetch/warmers rolled to affected pool (non-disruptive).
- Cross-pool streaming routing for new sessions.
- Extra monitoring on cache hit-rate, scheduler latencies, and streaming handshake RTTs.

Permanent mitigations under work: 
- Kernel upgrade and deterministic eviction policy testing for the affected pool.
- Scheduler fix to ensure streaming session precedence while preserving throughput.
- Expanded synthetic tests for long-context streaming under realistic production mixes.

FAQ (short):
Q: Were any customer data or outputs lost?
A: No evidence of data loss. Some in-flight sessions experienced stalls; those sessions should be retried. We offer replay support for affected requests.

Q: Will my billing be impacted?
A: We will evaluate whether customers experienced measurable service degradation and propose credits on a case-by-case basis. Open a support ticket if you believe you should receive an SLA credit.

Q: Is this related to the April rollout of the new batching kernel?
A: Not directly — the April rollout targeted short-sequence throughput and was validated. This incident is the product of an emergent interaction between eviction policy and a localized kernel variant; we’ll include any relation in the RCA.

Internal notes / reminders (do not include in statuspage copy without edit):
- Follow up with eng-serving-runtime to get exhaustive kernel + eviction traces (JIRA-INC-9482).
- Prepare a brief technical addendum for product-hosted-api and dedicated customers who pin models/versions.
- Customer-success to prepare 1:1 outreach list for tenants that reported stalls in support intake.

Draft short statuspage blurb (sized for Statuspage):
- Title: Intermittent streaming latency in us-west (resolved for most)
- Body: Between 09:23–12:10 UTC on 2026-05-14 some streaming sessions in our us-west region experienced elevated tail latency and occasional stalls. We deployed mitigations (cache warming and temporary cross-pool routing); monitoring returned to baseline by 12:10 UTC. If you saw stalled sessions, please try reconnecting. We are publishing a full RCA within 5 business days and can assist with replays on request.

Suggested customer-facing attachments/links:
- Short how-to: replay requests (CONFLUENCE-Page-ID-12345)
- Incident ticket for trace sharing (JIRA-INC-9482)
notes_to_self: Keep statuspage note concise; postmortem should include graphs (p95/p99, cache hit-rate, eviction rate), scheduler traces, and per-pool kernel versions. Carlos to own the addendum; Maya to compile tenant outreach list. Tag eng-serving-runtime and product-hosted-api on final RCA.
